Auth.//: Admin sign-in. SigningKey is a secret and is deliberately NOT here. Set it with: dotnet user-secrets set "Auth:SigningKey" "..." --project KFC   (or the Auth__SigningKey environment variable in production).
Auth.// SigningKey: A long random string, 32 characters minimum. It is what makes an admin token impossible to forge. Anyone holding it can mint tokens for your admin screens, so treat it like a password. Changing it signs everyone out.
Auth.// Registration: There is no setup code. /api/auth/register works only while no admin account exists, and refuses once yours is created. Create your account as soon as the site is running.

Chat.//: Settings for the AI assistant. The API key is deliberately NOT here - it is stored with `dotnet user-secrets set "Chat:ApiKey" "..." --project KFC` in development, or the Chat__ApiKey environment variable in production. Anything in this file can end up in source control.
Chat.// Provider: Currently pointed at Groq, which has a free tier. The key for whichever provider you choose goes in user secrets, NOT here. To switch, change BaseUrl and Model together - each provider names its models differently. OpenAI (paid): BaseUrl "" and Model gpt-4o-mini. Groq (free): https://api.groq.com/openai/v1 - check console.groq.com for current model names, they change; openai/gpt-oss-120b and openai/gpt-oss-20b work today. OpenRouter (free models): https://openrouter.ai/api/v1 with meta-llama/llama-3.3-70b-instruct:free. Ollama (free, runs on your own PC, wants ~4GB RAM): http://localhost:11434/v1 with llama3.2 and any non-empty ApiKey.

OfficialFeed.//: No authorized machine-readable rate feed exists for Larkana today. The Sindh AMIS portal publishes rates as HTML only, with no API and no file download, so there is no URL to put here. Set Enabled and Url when an authorized feed becomes available - no code change is needed. Keep ApiKey out of source control; use dotnet user-secrets or an environment variable.
